title: Arakhin 31
description: Two baraitot on borrowing to redeem a field, then a new mishna on houses in walled cities: redeemable at once and for a full year, the debate over how that year is counted, why the refund is “like interest” but not interest, who keeps the house after a resale, a consecrated house, and Hillel’s enactment for a buyer who hides.
topics: 💰 Borrowing to redeem and redeeming in halves: the Rabbis against Rabbi Shimon
🏰 Houses in walled cities: redeem at once, for twelve months, then in perpetuity
📅 “Days”, “until the completion of the year of its sale” and “full”: Rabbi and the Rabbis on counting the year
⚖️ “Like a form of interest, but not interest”: a conditional sale of a field and uncertain interest
🔁 Sold on to a second buyer: whose year counts, and who keeps the house
🗓️ Rabbi Abba bar Memel on two houses, and two lambs, in First and Second Adar
🎁 A gift as well as a sale, and a consecrated house that can always be redeemed
🚪 The buyer who hid on the last day, and Hillel’s enactment of the Temple chamber

a1.he: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: לֹוֶה וְגוֹאֵל וְגוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵינוֹ לֹוֶה וְגוֹאֵל וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין. לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבָּנַן וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר בֵּית בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה — הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹאֵל מִיָּד, וְגוֹאֵל כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, הֲרֵי זֶה כְּמִין רִבִּית, וְאֵינוֹ רִבִּית.

a3.he: מֵת הַמּוֹכֵר — יִגְאַל בְּנוֹ, מֵת הַלּוֹקֵחַ — יִגְאַל מִיַּד בְּנוֹ. אֵין מוֹנִין שָׁנָה אֶלָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמָּכַר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַד מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה״.

a4.he: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״תְּמִימָה״, לְהָבִיא אֶת חֹדֶשׁ הָעִיבּוּר. רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לִיתֵּן לוֹ שָׁנָה וְעִיבּוּרָהּ. הִגִּיעַ יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה — הָיְתָה חֲלוּטָה לוֹ. אֶחָד הַלּוֹקֵחַ וְאֶחָד הַנִּיתָּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לַצְּמִיתוּת״.

a5.he: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״יָמִים״ — אֵין יָמִים פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם.

a6.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״יָמִים״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם. וְרַבִּי, מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם מְנָא לֵיהּ? נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״עַד תּוֹם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ״.

a7.he: וְרַבָּנַן? הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ, וְלֹא (שְׁנַת) [שָׁנָה] שֶׁל מִנְיַן עוֹלָם. וְיָמִים מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְמֵעֵת לְעֵת, דְּאִי מֵ״עַד תּוֹם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם — אִין, מֵעֵת לְעֵת — לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״יָמִים״.

a8.he: וְרַבִּי, מֵעֵת לְעֵת מְנָא לֵיהּ? נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״תְּמִימָה״. וְרַבָּנַן? הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְעִיבּוּרַהּ.

a9.he: וְרַבִּי נָמֵי, הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְעִיבּוּרַהּ! הָכִי נָמֵי, מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם וּמֵעֵת לְעֵת מֵ״עַד תּוֹם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ״ נָפְקָא.

a10.he: הֲרֵי זוֹ כְּמִין רִבִּית וְכוּ׳. וְהָתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי זוֹ רִבִּית גְּמוּרָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה הִתִּירַתּוּ!

a11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְהָא רַבָּנַן. דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה נוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה, וְעָשָׂה לוֹ שָׂדֵהוּ מֶכֶר, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַמּוֹכֵר אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת — מוּתָּר, לוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת — אָסוּר.

a12.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַלּוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת — מוּתָּר. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבַיְתוֹס בֶּן זוֹנִין שֶׁעָשָׂה שָׂדֵהוּ מֶכֶר עַל פִּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, וְלוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת הָיָה. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָיה? מוֹכֵר אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת הָיָה, וְלֹא לוֹקֵחַ.

a13.he: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית מוּתָּר.

b1.he: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר, וְהָכָא בְּרִבִּית עַל מְנָת לְהַחְזִיר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ — מָר סָבַר: אָסוּר, וּמָר סָבַר: מוּתָּר.

b2.he: מֵת הַמּוֹכֵר יִגְאַל בְּנוֹ. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהַאי לָאו מְכַר, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן: ״וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ״ — מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

b3.he: מֵת הַלּוֹקֵחַ יִגְאַל מִיָּד בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: ״לַקּוֹנֶה אוֹתוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָא לָא קְנָה — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: ״וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ״ מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

b4.he: אֵין מוֹנִין לוֹ שָׁנָה אֶלָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמָּכַר כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁנָה — אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם שָׁנָה לָרִאשׁוֹן אִם שָׁנָה לַשֵּׁנִי, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״עַד מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה״ — הֱוֵי שָׁנָה לָרִאשׁוֹן.

b5.he: לְמִי חָלוּט? רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לָרִאשׁוֹן חָלוּט, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לַשֵּׁנִי חָלוּט. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דִּלְדִידֵיהּ קָא מָנֵינַן, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: מָה מָכַר לוֹ רִאשׁוֹן לְשֵׁנִי — כׇּל זְכוּת שֶׁתָּבֹא לְיָדוֹ.

b6.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: מָכַר שְׁנֵי בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה, אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאֶחָד בְּאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי; זֶה שֶׁמָּכַר לוֹ בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ יוֹם אֶחָד בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה — עָלְתָה לוֹ שָׁנָה; זֶה שֶׁמָּכַר לוֹ בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שֶׁל אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן — לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ שָׁנָה עַד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה.

b7.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: ״אֲנָא קָדֵים שָׁחֵין נוּרָא מִקַּמֵּא דִּידָךְ״! מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״אַתְּ נְחֵית לְעִיבּוּרָא״.

b8.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי טְלָאִים, אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שֶׁל אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאֶחָד בְּאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי, זֶה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ יוֹם אֶחָד בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה — עָלְתָה לוֹ שָׁנָה, זֶה שֶׁנּוֹלַד לוֹ בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן — לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ שָׁנָה עַד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה.

b9.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: אֲנָא קָדֵים אָכֵיל יְרוּקָּא מִקַּמָּךְ דִּידָךְ! מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ נְחֵיתְתְּ לְעִיבּוּרָא, אֲנָא לָא נְחֵיתְנָא לְעִיבּוּרָא.

b10.he: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הַיְינוּ הָךְ! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם, דִּכְתִיב ״תְּמִימָה״, הָכָא, דְּלָא כְּתִיב ״תְּמִימָה״ — לָא. קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּ״שָׁנָה״ ״שָׁנָה״ מֵהֲדָדֵי גָּמְרִי.

b11.he: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״תְּמִימָה״ כּוּ׳. רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לִיתֵּן שְׁנַת עִיבּוּרָהּ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״שָׁנָה תְּמִימָה״, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה יָמִים כְּמִנְיַן יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם, וְאִם נִתְעַבְּרָה — נִתְעַבְּרָה לוֹ.

b12.he: הִגִּיעַ יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא נִגְאָל כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לַצְּמִיתוּת״ — לַחֲלוּטִין. דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״לַצְּמִיתוּת״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַמַּתָּנָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? ״צְמִית״ ״צְמִיתוּת״.

b13.he: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר — הָאָמַר מַתָּנָה אֵינָהּ כְּמֶכֶר! אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, שָׁאנֵי הָכָא דְּרַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״לַצְּמִיתוּת״.

b14.he: אֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב פָּפָּא, וַאֲמַר לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא: וְהָא גַּבֵּי יוֹבֵל, דִּכְתִיב ״תָּשׁוּבוּ״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַמַּתָּנָה, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא קָא מְרַבֵּי! אֶלָּא הָא וַדַּאי דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.

b15.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה — הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹאֵל, וְגוֹאֵל לְעוֹלָם. גְּאָלוֹ אַחֵר מִיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ, הִגִּיעַ יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא נִגְאַל — הָיָה חָלוּט לוֹ.

b16.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לַקּוֹנֶה אוֹתוֹ״, וַאֲפִילּוּ מִיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ. וְלַחְלְטֵיהּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ? אָמַר קְרָא: ״לְדוֹרוֹתָיו״, יָצָא הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דּוֹרוֹת.

b17.he: לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיּוֹבֵל, לְמָה לִי? אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְמוֹכֵר בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה, וּפָגַע בּוֹ יוֹבֵל בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לִיפּוֹק בְּיוֹבֵל, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: ״לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיּוֹבֵל״.

b18.he: מַתְנִי׳ בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה נִטְמָן יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא חָלוּט לוֹ. הִתְקִין הִלֵּל שֶׁיְּהֵא חוֹלֵשׁ מְעוֹתָיו לַלִּשְׁכָּה, וִיהֵא שׁוֹבֵר אֶת הַדֶּלֶת וְנִכְנָס, אֵימָתַי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה הַלָּז יָבֹא וְיִטּוֹל אֶת מְעוֹתָיו.

b19.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַלֵּל — ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״, וּנְתָנָהּ לוֹ מִדַּעְתּוֹ — מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — אֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת.

messages.text: Continued from 30b: Rabbi Shimon explained why one who sells his ancestral field may not borrow money to redeem it or redeem it partially, while one who consecrates his ancestral field may do both.
The Gemara raises a contradiction between two baraitot with regard to redeeming a field from the Temple treasury: It is taught in one baraita:
One may borrow money and redeem a field, and one may partially redeem it.

notes.he: במקדיש שדה אחוזה לוה וגואל היינו הך דקתני לעיל אם גאל יגאל מלמד שלוה וגואל כו' ור"ש קאמר לה ואידך רבנן דפליגי עליה:
notes.en: It is taught in one [baraita]: [This refers] to one who consecrates an ancestral field. “He may borrow and redeem” is the same as what was taught above [30b]: “If he will indeed redeem” teaches that he may borrow and redeem, etc.; and Rabbi Shimon states it. And the other [baraita] is the Rabbis, who disagree with him.

notes.he: פירש רש"י דאמקדיש שדה אחוזה קאי ול"נ דא"כ הוי סתם מתני' דתנן בהקדש מותר בכולן כר"ש ולא כרבנן ואור"י דקאי אמוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה וכן מוכחת הסוגיא בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כא. ושם כ:) אבל מקדיש שדה אחוזה אפי' רבנן מודו דלוה וגואל לחצאין:
notes.en: It is taught in one [baraita]: one may borrow and redeem, [and redeem] partially: Rashi explained that it refers to one who consecrates an ancestral field. But this does not seem right to me, for if so, the unattributed mishna [30b] that teaches “but with regard to the Temple, it is permitted in all of them” would follow Rabbi Shimon and not the Rabbis. And the Ri said that it refers to one who sells a house among the houses of walled cities, and so the discussion in the first chapter of Kiddushin (21a, and there 20b) proves. But with regard to one who consecrates an ancestral field, even the Rabbis agree that one may borrow and redeem, and redeem partially.

notes.he: [לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין] אמוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה קאי דהכי משמע במסכ' קידושין:
notes.en: It is taught in one [baraita]: one may borrow and redeem, and redeem partially: this refers to one who sells a house among the houses of walled cities, for so it is implied in tractate Kiddushin.

messages.text: And it is taught in another baraita:
One may not borrow money and redeem a field, nor may one partially redeem it.

It is not difficult. This baraita, which teaches that one may not borrow money and redeem his field, is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis; and that baraita, which states that one may borrow money and redeem his field, is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who is lenient with regard to redeeming a field from the Temple treasury.

notes.he: הא דתני לוה וגואל לחצאין ר' שמעון היא [דכי היכי] דאמר לפי שמצינו [מקום שהורע כחו בענין אחד יפה כוחו בענין אחר] הכא נמי (הורע כחו בבתי ערי חומה בענין אחד) [במוכר בית בערי חומה הואיל והורע כחו] שאם הגיע (יום) שנים עשר חדש ולא היה נגאל היה חלוט לו ללוקח יפה כחו בענין אחר שלוה וגואל והא דתני אינו לוה וגואל רבנן היא דפליגי עליה דר' שמעון דלית להו לפי שמצינו כו':
notes.en: This is the Rabbis and that is Rabbi Shimon: the one that teaches “he may borrow and redeem, partially” is Rabbi Shimon. [Just as] he said, “Because we find [that where his power was diminished in one respect, his power was enhanced in another respect],” so here too, [with one who sells a house in a walled city, since his power was diminished,] in that if twelve months arrived and it was not redeemed, it became permanently the buyer’s, his power is enhanced in another respect, in that he may borrow and redeem. And the one that teaches “he may not borrow and redeem” is the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Shimon and do not hold “because we find,” etc.

notes.he: תניא בת"כ גבי מוכר שדה אחוזה וחשב שני ממכרו שנים אתה מחשב ואי אתה מחשב חדשים ומנין אם רצה לעשות חדשים שנה יעשה ת"ל וחשב וא"ת היכי מצינו ששניהם לצורך המוכר שיהא בו ריוח למוכר בשלמא כשמחשב חדשים מצינו כגון שבא לגאלה באמצע השנה דמחשבינן ליה חדשים שעברו שאכל הלוקח לגרע פדיונו כמו שאנו מחשבין השנים שעברו שאכל הלוקח אבל אי אתה מחשב חדשים היכי משכחת לה ויש לומר דמשכחת ליה כגון אם מכר בניסן בעשרה ליטרין ומחצה ויש עד היובל י' שנים ומחצה ובא לגואלה בר"ה ויש עוד להבא עד היובל ה' שנים:
notes.en: It is taught in the Torat Kohanim regarding one who sells an ancestral field: “And he shall reckon the years of its sale” (Leviticus 25:27): you reckon years, but you do not reckon months. And from where [is it derived that] if he wished to make months [count as] a year, he may do so? The verse states: “And he shall reckon.” And if you say: how do we find that both are for the seller’s need, so that there is gain for the seller? Granted, when he reckons months, we find it, e.g., where he comes to redeem it in the middle of the year, that we reckon for him the months that have passed, which the buyer consumed, to reduce his redemption price, just as we reckon the years that have passed, which the buyer consumed. But “you do not reckon months,” how do you find [that this is for his gain]? One can say that you find it, e.g., where he sold in Nisan for ten and a half litra, and there were ten and a half years until the Jubilee, and he comes to redeem it on Rosh HaShana, and there are five more years to come until the Jubilee.

messages.text: Mishna

One who sells a house from among the houses of walled cities may redeem the house immediately, even without the consent of the buyer, and he may redeem the house during the entire twelve months following the sale, but not after that.

notes.he: ואין לו דין שדה אחוזה שצריך להמתין שתי שנים:
notes.en: Mishna. He may redeem immediately: and it does not have the law of an ancestral field, where he must wait two years.

notes.he: אפי' לאלתר כשמכר:
notes.en: He may redeem immediately: even right away, when he sold it.

messages.text: When he redeems the house within the twelve-month period, he returns the sale price to the buyer, and this is ostensibly like a form of interest, as the buyer has effectively resided in the house for free in exchange for the fact that the buyer’s money was in the possession of the seller. It is not considered interest, because the buyer owned the house during the period in which he resided in it.

notes.he: שכשמחזיר לו מעותיו בתוך שנה ואין זה מנכה לו כלום נמצא שנשתמש בביתו בשכר המתנת מעותיו:
notes.en: This is like a form of interest: for when he returns his money to him within the year, and this one [the buyer] deducts nothing for him, it turns out that he used his house in return for waiting for his money.

notes.he: גמורה דרבית לא מיקרי אלא ע"י הלואה ולא ע"י מכר:
notes.en: And it is not interest: full [interest], for it is called interest only when it comes through a loan, and not through a sale.

notes.he: שאם היה ביד הלוקח חצי שנה [או] ח' חדשים אינו מנכה לו הלוקח לגואל כלום ממה שאכל והיינו כמין רבית שלוקח כל דמיו ואינו מנכה לו]:
notes.en: This is like a form of interest: for if it was in the buyer’s hand for half a year [or] eight months, the buyer deducts nothing for the redeemer from what he consumed. And this is like a form of interest, that he takes all his money and deducts nothing for him.

notes.he: שאינו מחסרו כלום שהתורה זיכתה לו:
notes.en: And it is not interest: for he causes him no loss at all, since the Torah granted it to him.

messages.text: If the seller died, his son may redeem the house from the buyer.

notes.he: בתוך שנה אם ירצה אבל לאחר שנה נחלט ואינו נגאל עוד לעולם כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ל׳) ואם לא יגאל עד מלאת לו שנה וגו':
notes.en: His son may redeem: within the year, if he wishes; but after a year it becomes permanent and is never redeemed again, as it is written: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him,” etc. (Leviticus 25:30).

messages.text: If the buyer died, the seller may redeem it from the possession of the buyer’s son.

If the buyer sold the house to another, one calculates the year only from the time that the owner sold the house to the first buyer, as it is stated: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him, then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30). The term “for him” indicates that the year is calculated from when the initial owner sold the house.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: שאם מכרה ראובן לשמעון בניסן ושמעון ללוי באייר כיון שהגיע ניסן הבא נחלט ואין מונין למכר שני אלא לראשון:
notes.en: Only from the time that it was sold: for if Reuven sold it to Shimon in Nisan, and Shimon [sold it] to Levi in Iyyar, once the next Nisan arrives it becomes permanent. One does not count for the second sale, but for the first.

notes.he: משמע לזה שהיתה אחוזה שלו מונין:
notes.en: As it is stated: “Until the passage of a full year for him”: implying that one counts for this one, whose ancestral holding it was.

notes.he: למכירתו:
notes.en: Until the passage of a full year for him: [that is,] for his sale.

messages.text: When it says: “A full year,” this serves to include the intercalated month in the year calculated from the sale, if it was a leap year.

notes.he: שאם היתה שנה מעוברת אינה נחלטת עד שלשה עשר חדש:
notes.en: The intercalated month: so that if it was a leap year, it does not become permanent until thirteen months [have passed].

messages.text: The word “full” serves to give the seller a year and its addition, i.e., the year during which the house may be redeemed is not the 354-day lunar year, but the 365-day solar year.

notes.he: בין בשנה פשוטה בין בשנה מעוברת נותנין לו שנת לבנה וימים שיתירים בשנת חמה על שנת לבנה אחד עשר יום שמהם אנו מעברים את השנה:
notes.en: A year and its addition: whether in an ordinary year or in a leap year, we give him a lunar year and the days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year, eleven days, on account of which we intercalate the year.

notes.he: (שס"ה היינו עיבורה י"א יום שיתירה שנת חמה על הלבנה) היינו שנת הלבנה ומה שיתירים חדשי החמה על חדשי הלבנה דהיינו י"א יום דהיינו שס"ה ימים שתהא תמימה בין ללבנה ובין לחמה:
notes.en: A year and its addition: (365; that is, its addition is the eleven days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year.) That is, the lunar year and the amount by which the months of the sun exceed the months of the moon, eleven days, which makes 365 days, so that it is full both by the moon and by the sun.

messages.text: If the final day of the twelve-month period arrived and the house was not redeemed, the house has become the property of the buyer in perpetuity. This is the halakha with regard to both one who buys a house in a walled city and one to whom it is given as a gift, as it is stated: “Then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30).

notes.he: אם רצה נותן לגאול בתוך שנתו יגאל ואם לאו חלוט לו:
notes.en: And one to whom it is given as a gift: if the giver wishes to redeem it within its year, he may redeem it; and if not, it is permanently his [the recipient’s].

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דקתני הרי זה גואל מיד דמשמע אפי' בו ביום שמכרה מותר לגאול דלא כרבי:
notes.en: Gemara. The mishna: which teaches “he may redeem immediately,” implying that he may redeem it even on the very day he sold it, is not in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].

notes.he: מתני' דתני הרי זה גואל מיד דלא כר' דתניא ימים תהיה גאולתו ר' אומר אין ימים פחות משנים. כלומר דקסבר המוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה אינו רשאי לגאול אלא לאחר שני ימים:
notes.en: The mishna, which teaches “he may redeem immediately,” is not in accordance with Rabbi, as it is taught: “For days he shall have the right of redemption”; Rabbi says: “Days” are no fewer than two. That is, he holds that one who sells a house among the houses of walled cities may not redeem it until after two days.

messages.text: The Torah states: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it until the completion of the year after it is sold; for days he shall have the right of redemption” (Leviticus 25:29). The word “days” means no fewer than two days, i.e., the house cannot be redeemed during the first two days after the sale.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִמְכֹּר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד־תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who sells a dwelling house in a walled city: It may be redeemed until a year has elapsed since its sale; the redemption period shall be a year.

notes.dh: ימים תהיה גאולתו ואין ימים פחותין משנים
notes.he: דלא תשהא ביד לוקח פחות משני ימים:
notes.en: “For days he shall have the right of redemption,” and “days” are no fewer than two: that it should not remain in the buyer’s hand for less than two days.

messages.text: And the Rabbis, what do they do with this word “days”?
messages.quote: The word “days” means no fewer than two days

notes.he: דסברי דגואל מיד האי ימים מאי עבדי ליה:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: who hold that he may redeem immediately, what do they do with this “days”?

messages.text: The Rabbis require it to teach the halakha that the year does not conclude with the arrival of Rosh HaShana, at the end of the calendar year; rather, it is calculated from day to day, that is, until the arrival of the date of the sale in the subsequent year.

notes.he: שגואל עד מלאות שנה מיום ליום וימים מבעי להו לשנה תמימה מעת לעת באותה שעה שמכרה:
notes.en: They need it: [to teach] that he may redeem until the passage of a year from day to day. And they need “days” for a full year from hour to hour, [counting to] the same hour at which he sold it.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, from where does he derive that the year is calculated from day to day?
He derives it from the phrase: “Until the completion of the year after it is sold” (Leviticus 25:29).

notes.he: נפקא מיום ליום ומעת לעת אייתר ליה ימים שאין ימים פחות משנים:
notes.en: From “until the completion of the year of its sale”: he derives from day to day and from hour to hour; “days” is left over for him, [to teach] that “days” are no fewer than two.

messages.text: And the Rabbis, what do they do with this phrase?
Actually, they require that phrase to teach that the calculated year is a year from his sale and not the year of the counting of the world, i.e., not the calendar year.

notes.he: שאין אומרים אם מכר לו באלול או באב כיון שהגיע יום א' בתשרי עלתה לו שנה אלא מונה שנה שלימה:
notes.en: And not a year of the world’s count: for we do not say that if he sold it to him in Elul or in Av, once the first day of Tishrei arrives a year has passed for him; rather, he counts a complete year.

messages.text: And the Rabbis require the word “days” to teach that the year is calculated not only from day to day, but also from hour to hour, i.e., the year is completed only when the hour of the sale arrives in the subsequent year.

As if one sought to derive this from the phrase “until the completion of the year after it is sold,” I would say that with regard to calculating the year from day to day, yes, it is calculated in this manner, but with regard to calculating the year from hour to hour, no, it is not calculated in this manner. Rather, once the beginning of the day arrives the seller can no longer redeem the house. The Merciful One therefore wrote the word “days” to teach that the year is calculated from hour to hour.

notes.he: כלומר דאם מכר לו בפסח ואותה שנה חל פסח ביום א' ולשנה הבאה חל פסח ביום ה' אין אומרים כיון שהגיע יום א' בניסן הבא דהוא יום [י"א] בחודש (א') עלתה לו שנה [מיום ליום] אלא אין עולה לו שנה עד שיגיע הפסח דהיינו מעת לעת:
notes.en: They need it for hour to hour: that is, if he sold it to him on Passover, and that year Passover fell on the first day of the week, and the next year Passover falls on the fifth day, we do not say that once the first day of the week in the next Nisan arrives, which is the [eleventh] of the month, a year has passed for him [from day to day]; rather, a year has not passed for him until Passover arrives, which is hour to hour.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, from where does he derive that the year is calculated from hour to hour?
He derives it from the term “a full year” (Leviticus 25:30).
And the Rabbis, what do they derive from the term “a full year”? The Rabbis require that term to teach that the intercalated month of a leap year is included in the year of sale.

notes.he: אין הכי נמי דההיא ודאי מיבעי ליה להכי דממכרו ולא שנת מנין עולם וימים מיבעי ליה למעת לעת שאם מכרה באחד בניסן בחצי היום אין מונין לו שנה עד שיגיע חצי היום של אחד בניסן הבא:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: indeed, that [phrase] is certainly needed for this: “of its sale,” and not the year of the world’s count. And “days” is needed for hour to hour: so that if he sold it on the first of Nisan at midday, one does not count a year for him until midday of the next first of Nisan arrives.

messages.text: But Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi also requires that term to teach that the intercalated month of a leap year is included in the year of sale.

Indeed, i.e., Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi derives the inclusion of the intercalated month from the term “a full year.” Rather, according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, the fact that the year is calculated from day to day and from hour to hour constitutes one halakha, which is derived from the phrase “until the completion of the year after it is sold.”

notes.he: שאם מכרה באחד בניסן אין מונין שנה למנין עולם דלימא כיון שהגיע תשרי עלתה לו שנה שהרי יצתה אותה שנה אלא עד אחד בניסן הבא אינו נחלט:
notes.en: From day to day: that if he sold it on the first of Nisan, one does not count the year by the world’s count, saying that once Tishrei arrives a year has passed for him, since that year has ended. Rather, it does not become permanent until the next first of Nisan.

notes.he: ולא של מנין עולם:
notes.en: The year of its sale: and not of the world’s count.

notes.dh: מיום ליום ומעת לעת מעד תום שנת ממכרו נפקא
notes.he: במס' נדה דף מז: ושם ד"ה כולן) פירש ה"ר ר' אלחנן דדוקא בבתי ערי חומה בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות] אבל אינך דהתם דמצי למימר דאזלינן בהן בתר שנים שלהם ולא בתר שנות עולם בכולהו לא בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות] דבבתי ערי חומה דוקא הוא דגלי ליה קרא אבל דאינך לא והתוס' כתבו כאן הוא הדין בכולהו בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות] דילפינן שנה [שנה] מבתי ערי חומה כדאמר הש"ס לקמן גבי מילתא אחריתי:
notes.en: From day to day and from hour to hour is derived from “until the completion of the year of its sale”: In tractate Niddah (47b, and there, s.v. kulan), Rabbi Elḥanan explained that only with houses of walled cities do we require [a year] from hour to hour; but with the other cases there, where one can say that we follow their own years and not the years of the world, in all of them we do not require hour to hour, for it is only with houses of walled cities that the verse revealed it, and not with the others. And the Tosafot wrote here that the same applies to all of them: we require hour to hour, since we derive “year” “year” from houses of walled cities, as the Gemara says below [31b] with regard to another matter.

notes.dh: מיום ליום ומעת לעת מעד שנת ממכרו נפקא
notes.he: אייתר ליה ימים ואין ימים פחות משנים:
notes.en: From day to day and from hour to hour is derived from “until the completion of the year of its sale”: “days” is left over for him, [to teach] that “days” are no fewer than two.

messages.caption: Three phrases of Leviticus 25:29–30 and what each one teaches, according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and according to the Rabbis, as the Gemara finally settles it.

messages.text: § When one redeems a house among those of a walled city, this is ostensibly like a form of interest, as the seller returns the original sale price to the buyer and he does not subtract from it in exchange for the period during which the buyer resided in the house. This is not considered interest because the buyer owned the house during that period. But isn’t it taught in a baraita: This is fully considered interest, but in this case the Torah permitted it?
messages.quote: this is ostensibly like a form of interest

notes.dh: והתניא הרי זו רבית גמורה אלא שהתורה התירתו
notes.he: ומסיק רבי יוחנן הא ר' יהודה הא רבנן פירוש מתני' כר' יהודה דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר וברייתא דתני רבית גמורה אתיא כרבנן וא"ת מאי שנא ממשכנתא בלא נכייתא דאינו אלא אבק רבית כדאיתא באיזהו נשך (ב"מ דף סב. ושם) א"ל רבינא והרי משכנתא בלא נכייתא דבדיניהם מוציאין מלוה למלוה ובדיננו אין מחזירין ממלוה ללוה אלמא לאו רבית גמורה היא והכא אמר דהוי ריבית גמורה ולפי פירוש רש"י דמחלק בין שדה לבית ניחא גבי הא דתנן פרק איזהו נשך (בבא מציעא סד:) המלוה את חבירו לא ידור בחצרו חנם ולא ישכור ממנו בפחות (ממנו) [מפני] שהוא רבית ופירש רש"י שם מאי שנא ממשכנתא דנכייתא דשרי ותירץ דיש לחלק בין שדה לבית דשמא השדה לא יעשה פירות אבל הבית אי אפשר שלא יהנה ממנו בדירתו ומשום הכי כי מנכה לו מן השכירות הוי רבית ולפי זה ניחא נמי הכא דבית שהוא דר בו בלא ספק הוי רבית גמורה אבל שדה דשמא לא יעשה פירות כי אכיל ליה נמי בלא נכייתא לאו רבית גמורה היא ואין נראה לר"ת חילוק זה דבבית נמי איכא ספיקא שמא יפול או ישרף אלא ודאי אין חילוק בין שדה לבית וההיא דמלוה את חבירו לא ישכור ממנו בפחות יש לתרץ דלא דמי למשכנתא בנכייתא דשרי דההיא משכנתא מיירי שהלוה לו על השדה ואין הלוה יכול להשכירו לאחר מפני שהוא ביד המלוה משום הכי אינו רבית דהא בלאו הכי הוא בטל והא דתנן המלוה את חבירו לא ישכור ממנו בפחות מיירי שלא הלוה לו על שדה או על הבית וביד הלוה להשכירו לאחר נמצא כשמוזיל גביה רבית הואי ולפי' זה דר"ת אינו מחלק בין שדה לבית הדרא קושיא לדוכתיה מאי שנא ממשכנתא בלא נכייתא דלא חשבינן ליה רבית גמורה וצ"ל דרבית גמורה מדרבנן קאמר והאי דאמר אלא שהתורה התירתו הכי פירושו מדכתב לן רחמנא דין בתי ערי חומה גלי לן דכי ה"ג אין זה רבית דאורייתא:
notes.en: In brief: Rabbi Yoḥanan concludes that the mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda, who permits one-sided interest, and the baraita that calls this “full interest” follows the Rabbis. Tosafot ask: how is this different from a mortgage without deduction [mashkanta be-lo nakhyata], which is only “the dust of interest,” as in Bava Metzia 62a, where Ravina says that by their laws one exacts [it] from lender to lender, and by our law one does not return [it] from lender to borrower, so it is not full interest; yet here it is called full interest? According to Rashi’s explanation, which distinguishes between a field and a house, this is resolved. On the mishna in Bava Metzia 64b, “one who lends to another may not live in his courtyard for free nor rent from him for less, because it is interest,” Rashi asked how this differs from a mortgage with deduction, which is permitted, and answered that a field may not produce, but one cannot fail to benefit from living in a house; so even when he deducts from the rent, it is interest. Accordingly, here too a house that he lives in is certainly full interest, while consuming a field’s produce, which may not grow, is not full interest even without deduction. Rabbeinu Tam rejects this distinction, since a house too is uncertain: it may fall or burn. Rather, there is no difference between field and house, and the mishna about renting for less is answered differently: the permitted mortgage with deduction is where he lent against the field, and the borrower could not rent it to another anyway, since it is in the lender’s hand; whereas “he may not rent from him for less” is where he did not lend against the field or the house, and the borrower could rent it to another, so a discount is interest. On Rabbeinu Tam’s view the question returns: why is a mortgage without deduction not considered full interest? One must say that “full interest” here means by rabbinic law, and “but the Torah permitted it” means that by writing the law of houses of walled cities, the Merciful One revealed that in such a case it is not interest by Torah law. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: It is not difficult. This mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, and that baraita is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר דרבית הבאה ע"י מכר קרי צד אחד משום דאין בא לידי רבית משני צדדין שאם לא יגאלנה ותיחלט לו אין כאן רבית אבל הלואה ודאי באה לידי רבית שאינה נחלטת לעולם:
notes.en: The mishna is Rabbi Yehuda: who says that one-sided interest is permitted. He calls interest that comes through a sale “one side,” because it does not come to interest from both sides: if he does not redeem it and it becomes permanently his, there is no interest here. But a loan certainly comes to interest, since it never becomes permanent [property of the lender].

messages.text: Consider the case of one who had a debt of one hundred dinars against another, and the borrower made a conditional sale of his field to the lender, stipulating that if he does not repay the loan on time then the sale shall take effect retroactively from the present moment.

notes.he: שמשכן לו שדהו על אותו מנה וכתב לו אם לא אתן לך מנה מיכן ועד שלש שנים הרי היא שלך:
notes.en: And made a sale of his field to him: he pledged his field to him for that maneh and wrote to him: If I do not give you a maneh from now until three years, it is yours.

notes.he: כשלוה ממנו אמר לו אם איני פורע לך מיכן ועד זמן פלוני תהא שדי מכורה לך מעכשיו בכך וכך ותחשוב בה דמיך ותחזיר לי המותר על חובך ועכשיו היא ברשות הלוקח:
notes.en: And made a sale of his field to him: when he borrowed from him, he said to him: If I do not repay you from now until such-and-such a time, my field shall be sold to you from now for such-and-such [a price], and you shall reckon your money in it and return to me whatever exceeds your debt. And now it is in the buyer’s possession.

messages.text: As long as the seller, i.e., the borrower, consumes the produce of that field until the time the loan comes due, this arrangement is permitted. But if the buyer, i.e., the lender, consumes the produce during this time, the arrangement is prohibited, as it constitutes interest. The reason is that if the loan is repaid on time, the sale is nullified, which means that the produce consumed by the lender will have been consumed as payment for allowing the loan to remain in the borrower’s possession.

notes.he: כל אותן שנים מותר:
notes.en: As long as the seller consumes the produce: all those years, it is permitted.

notes.he: שמא יגאלנה בתוך שלש ונמצא שאכלם ברבית:
notes.en: The buyer consumes the produce, prohibited: lest he redeem it within the three [years], and it turns out that he consumed them as interest.

notes.he: [בזמן שהמוכר אוכל הפירות עד אותו זמן מותר שעד הזמן היא שלו:
notes.en: As long as the seller consumes the produce until that time, it is permitted: for until that time it is his.

notes.he: דשמא יפדנה זה ונמצא לוקח אוכל רבית למפרע]:
notes.en: The buyer consumes the produce, prohibited: for perhaps this one [the borrower] will redeem it, and it will turn out that the buyer consumed interest retroactively.

messages.text: Even when the buyer consumes the produce, such an arrangement is permitted.
messages.quote: if the buyer, i.e., the lender, consumes the produce during this time, the arrangement is prohibited

notes.he: דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר דרבית הבאה ע"י מכר קרי צד אחד משום דאין בא לידי רבית משני צדדין שאם לא יגאלנה ותיחלט לו אין כאן רבית אבל הלואה ודאי באה לידי רבית שאינה נחלטת לעולם:
notes.en: The mishna is Rabbi Yehuda: who says that one-sided interest is permitted. He calls interest that comes through a sale “one side,” because it does not come to interest from both sides: if he does not redeem it and it becomes permanently his, there is no interest here. But a loan certainly comes to interest, since it never becomes permanent. [The same comment appears on the previous segment.]

notes.dh: ר' יהודה אומר אף בזמן שהלוקח אוכל פירות מותר
notes.he: הואיל ואינו תופשה בתורת משכון אלא בתורת מכר:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: even when the buyer consumes the produce it is permitted: since he does not hold it as a pledge, but as a sale.

messages.text: There was an incident involving Baitos ben Zunin, who made a conditional sale of his field by a similar arrangement under the direction of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and in this case the buyer was consuming the produce.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehuda said in support of his opinion:

notes.he: מעשה בביתוס בן זונין גרסינן:
notes.en: We read: “An incident involving Baitos ben Zonin.” [This is Rashi’s version of the text.]

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda Do you seek to bring proof from there? Actually, it was the seller who was consuming the produce, and not the buyer.
messages.quote: the buyer was consuming the produce

messages.text: What is the basis for the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis?

The dispute between them concerns the permissibility of an agreement involving an uncertain interest, i.e., an agreement that will involve interest only under certain circumstances. This is the case here, since if the loan is repaid the produce consumed by the lender constitutes interest, but if the loan is not repaid then the field is acquired retroactively by the lender and no interest is involved.

notes.he: שאם יגאלנה יהא רבית ואם לאו לא יהא רבית:
notes.en: One-sided interest: that if he redeems it, it will be interest, and if not, it will not be interest.

notes.he: להכי קרי ליה צד אחד ברבית דלא חשיב רבית [גמורה] אלא רבית דהלואה כגון הלוהו סלע בה' דינרין אבל רבית דמקח וממכר קרי צד אחד רבית ואיכא דאמר היינו צד אחד ברבית שאם יפדנו יהא רבית מה שאכל ואם לא יפדנו לא יהא רבית:
notes.en: The difference between them is one-sided interest: it is called “one-sided interest” because only the interest of a loan, such as lending a sela for five dinars, is considered [full] interest; but interest through buying and selling is called one-sided interest. And some say: this is one-sided interest, that if he redeems it, what he consumed will be interest, and if he does not redeem it, it will not be interest.

messages.text: The first tanna, i.e., the Rabbis, holds that uncertain interest is prohibited, and Rabbi Yehuda holds that uncertain interest is permitted.

notes.dh: ור' יהודה סבר צד אחד ברבית מותר
notes.he: וא"ת לר' יהודה משכנתא בלא נכייתא נמי תישתרי דצד אחד בריבית הוא ושמא לא יפדנו עוד וי"ל דלא חשבינן צד אחד ברבית אלא כגון עשה לו שדהו מכר דאיכא צד מכר אם לא יפדנו בתוך הזמן הקבוע לו אבל משכנתא בלא נכייתא דליכא ביה צד מכר דלעולם הוא ביד הלוה לפדותו ואם יפדנו כיון שאין מנכה לו מן הפירות שאכל הוה ליה רבית מידי דהוה אמלוה סאה בסאה ולא חשיב ליה ר' יהודה צד אחד ברבית אף על גב דשמא לא יתייקר מ"מ כיון דאין בו צד מכר אסור ולא חשיב ליה ר"י צד אחד ברבית:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda holds that one-sided interest is permitted: And if you say: according to Rabbi Yehuda, let a mortgage without deduction also be permitted, since it is one-sided interest, for perhaps he will never redeem it. One can say: we consider it one-sided interest only in a case like “he made a sale of his field to him,” where there is a side of sale if he does not redeem it within the time fixed for him. But a mortgage without deduction has no side of sale, since it is always in the borrower’s power to redeem it; and if he redeems it, since he does not deduct for him the produce he consumed, it is interest. It is just like one who lends a se’a for a se’a, which Rabbi Yehuda does not consider one-sided interest: even though perhaps [the price] will not rise, nevertheless, since there is no side of sale in it, it is prohibited, and Rabbi Yehuda does not consider it one-sided interest.

messages.text: Everyone agrees that uncertain interest is prohibited; and here, the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis concerns the permissibility of interest given on the condition that it will be returned. That is, in addition to the arrangement described in the baraita, the parties agreed that the buyer will consume the produce, and if the sale will later be nullified, then the buyer will reimburse the seller for the value of the produce.
messages.quote: Rabbi Yehuda holds that uncertain interest is permitted

notes.he: כי ה"ג אסור הואיל ומעיקרא בתורת הלואה אתא לידיה ור' יהודה (דקאמר) [דקשרי] בהכי עסקינן שהתנו מתחילה שאם יגאלנה המוכר בתוך שלש יחזיר לו הלוקח הדמים מפירות שאכל וברבית ע"מ להחזיר פליגי ומתני' ותנא דברייתא בהא פליגי דתנא דידן סבר אפי' צד אחד נמי לא הוי דהא בתורת מכר אתא לידיה ותנא דברייתא סבר סוף סוף הואיל ולידי ריבית (לגבי) [אתי] צד אחד (היא) כרבית גמורה היא אלא שהתורה התירתה:
notes.en: Everyone agrees that one-sided interest: in this way is prohibited, since it originally came into his hand by way of a loan. And where Rabbi Yehuda permits, we are dealing with a case where they stipulated at the outset that if the seller redeems it within the three [years], the buyer will return to him the value of the produce that he consumed; and they disagree about interest on condition that it be returned. And the mishna and the tanna of the baraita disagree about this: our tanna holds that it is not even one-sided [interest], since it came into his hand by way of a sale; and the tanna of the baraita holds that in the end, since it comes to interest, it is one-sided [interest] and is like full interest, except that the Torah permitted it.

notes.dh: רבא אמר דכולי עלמא צד אחד ברבית אסור
notes.he: פירש"י ומתני' וברייתא בהא פליגי דתנא דברייתא סבר סוף סוף הואיל ולידי הרבית (לגבי) [אתי] צד אחד ברבית וכרבית גמורה היא אלא שהתורה התירתו [לשון] רש"י ועוד יש לפרש דבהכי פליגי מתני' וברייתא כגון שנכנס בבית להחזיר לו דמי שכירות שנה אם בא לפדותו בתוך י"ב חדש דתנא דמתני' סבר רבית על מנת להחזיר שרי ותנא דברייתא סבר דאסור אי נמי מר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי דמתני' מיירי כשמחזיר לו אם יפדנו וברייתא מיירי כשאין מחזיר:
notes.en: Rava said: Everyone agrees that one-sided interest is prohibited: Rashi explained that the mishna and the baraita disagree about this: the tanna of the baraita holds that in the end, since it comes to interest, it is one-sided interest and is like full interest, except that the Torah permitted it; [that is] Rashi’s wording. And one may further explain that the mishna and the baraita disagree about this: for example, where he entered the house [on condition] to return to him the rent for a year if he comes to redeem it within twelve months; the tanna of the mishna holds that interest on condition that it be returned is permitted, and the tanna of the baraita holds that it is prohibited. Alternatively, one [tanna] said one thing and the other said another, and they do not disagree: the mishna speaks of where he returns [the rent] to him if he redeems it, and the baraita of where he does not return it.

messages.text: One Sage, the first tanna, holds that although the interest is subsequently refunded, this practice is prohibited, and one Sage, Rabbi Yehuda, holds that this is permitted.

notes.dh: והכא ברבית ע"מ להחזיר איכא בינייהו
notes.he: שהלוה התנה עם המלוה שאם יכול לפורעו בזמנו שיחזיר לו שדהו רבנן סברי כיון שהתנה הלוה שתחזור השדה לידו הפירות שאכל [הלוקח] הרי זה רבית ור' יהודה סבר כיון שעשאה לו מכר קנאה המלוה קנין גמור עד אותו הזמן ומותר הוא הלוקח לאכול פירותיה שהיא שלו וחזרה זו שמחזירה לו המלוה אינו דומה כחזרה אלא דומה כמו שחוזר ומכרה לו המלוה עכשיו (דמי) הלכך לא הוי רבית ומתני' דקתני אינה רבית ר' יהודה היא. ע"א לשון מורי הגאון רבית ע"מ להחזיר שהתנה שאם יפדה את השדה שיחשוב לו דמי פירות שאכל ר' יהודה סבר כיון שמחזיר לו דמי הפירות מותר:
notes.en: And here the difference between them is interest on condition that it be returned: that the borrower stipulated with the lender that if he can repay him on time, he will return his field to him. The Rabbis hold that since the borrower stipulated that the field return to his hand, the produce that [the buyer] consumed is interest. And Rabbi Yehuda holds that since he made it a sale to him, the lender acquired it with a complete acquisition until that time, and the buyer is permitted to consume its produce, since it is his; and this return, in which the lender returns it to him, is not like a return but like the lender now selling it back to him. Therefore it is not interest, and the mishna, which teaches “it is not interest,” is Rabbi Yehuda. Another version, in the words of my teacher the Gaon: interest on condition that it be returned means that he stipulated that if he redeems the field, he will credit him the value of the produce he consumed; Rabbi Yehuda holds that since he returns to him the value of the produce, it is permitted.

messages.text: This is obvious, as a son inherits his father’s property.
messages.quote: the seller died, his son may redeem

messages.text: Lest you say that when the Merciful One states: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it until the completion of the year after it is sold” (Leviticus 25:29), this indicates that the man who redeems the house must be the same man who sold it, and this son did not sell; therefore, the same verse teaches us: “And he shall have the right of redemption,” indicating that the right of redemption applies in any case, either to the seller or his son.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִמְכֹּר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד־תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who sells a dwelling house in a walled city: It may be redeemed until a year has elapsed since its sale; the redemption period shall be a year.

notes.he: (איש כי ימכר אמר רחמנא):
notes.en: (“And if a man sells,” the Merciful One said.)

notes.he: משמע דא"כ הוה ליה למיכתב יגאלנה עד תום שנת ממכרו מדשני בדיבוריה וכתב והיתה גאולתו משמע אפי' ע"י אחר:
notes.en: “And he shall have the right of redemption,” in any case: implying that, if [only the seller could redeem], it should have written “he shall redeem it until the completion of the year of its sale”; since it changed its wording and wrote “and his redemption shall be,” this implies even by another.

notes.dh: איש כי ימכור אמר רחמנא והיתה גאולתו
notes.he: כלומר מי שמכר יגאול קמ"ל:
notes.en: “And if a man sells,” the Merciful One said, “and he shall have the right of redemption”: that is, [lest you say] the one who sold [is the one who] redeems; it teaches us [otherwise].

messages.text: This, too, is obvious.
messages.quote: the buyer died, the seller may redeem it from the possession of the buyer’s son

messages.text: Lest you say that the Merciful One states: “Then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30), and as this son did not buy the house, the buyer cannot redeem it from him; therefore, the previous verse teaches us: “He shall have the right of redemption,” indicating that this right applies in any case, even from the buyer’s son.

notes.he: משמע לקונה יהא נחלט אם לא יגאל בתוך שנה הא אם יגאל יחזירנה וקונה הוא דיחזירנה אבל בנו לא קמ"ל והיתה גאולתו מ"מ:
notes.en: “To the one who bought it”: implies that for the buyer it becomes permanent if it is not redeemed within a year; hence, if it is redeemed, he must return it. And it is the buyer who must return it, but not his son. [The verse] teaches us “and he shall have the right of redemption,” in any case.

messages.text: When the verse states “year,” I do not know if one counts the year from when the owner sold it to the first buyer, or if one counts the year from when the first buyer sold it to the second. When the verse states: “Until the passage of a full year for him,” you must say that it is a year from when the owner sold it to the first buyer.
messages.quote: one calculates the year only from the time that the owner sold the house to the first buyer

notes.he: אי הוה כתיב עד מלאת שנה ולא כתב לו איני יודע אם שנה למכר ראשון או שנה למכר שני כגון מכרה ראובן לשמעון בניסן ושמעון ללוי בתשרי וה"א ראובן שמכרה ראשון מחשב עם לוי ויהא לו רשות לגאלה עד תשרי הבא השתא דכתיב לו משמע דאמוכר ראשון קא מהדר:
notes.en: Year: if it had written “until the passage of a year” and had not written “for him,” I would not know whether [it means] a year for the first sale or a year for the second sale. For example, Reuven sold it to Shimon in Nisan, and Shimon [sold it] to Levi in Tishrei; I would say that Reuven, who sold it first, reckons with Levi and has the right to redeem it until the next Tishrei. Now that it writes “for him,” it implies that it refers back to the first seller.

notes.he: דכתיב ואם לא יגאל עד מלאת לו שנה איני יודע אם שנה לראשון אם שנה לשני כלומר שאם מכרה הלוקח לאחר אחר חצי שנה שקנאה איני יודע אם נלך אחר מלאת שנה של לוקח ראשון או של לוקח שני:
notes.en: Year: as it is written, “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him,” I do not know whether [it means] a year for the first or a year for the second. That is, if the buyer sold it to another half a year after he bought it, I do not know whether we follow the passage of the year of the first buyer or of the second buyer.

messages.text: In such a case, if the owner did not redeem the house within one year of the first sale, to whom does it belong in perpetuity?

notes.he: כשהגיע שנה למוכר ראשון ונחלט מי מן הלוקחים זוכה בחליטה זו:
notes.en: To whom is it permanent: when a year has arrived for the first seller and it has become permanent, which of the buyers acquires this permanence?

messages.text: It belongs in perpetuity to the first buyer.

notes.he: דראובן אין גואלה עוד משמעון אבל שמעון גואלה מלוי עד שיגיע שנה למכר שני שהרי ללוי לא נחלטה:
notes.en: It is permanent for the first: for Reuven can no longer redeem it from Shimon; but Shimon can redeem it from Levi until a year arrives for the second sale, for it has not become permanent for Levi.

notes.dh: כשהוא אומר עד מלאת לו למוכר ראשון קאמר
notes.he: למי חלוט אם לא גאלו מוכר ראשון עד מלאת שנה ר' אלעזר אמר ללוקח ראשון הוא חלוט] דלדידיה מנינן [למוכר] ללוקח ראשון מונין לו י"ב חדש הלכך בדין הוא שתהא חלוטה לו:
notes.en: When it says “until the passage of a year for him,” it speaks of the first seller. To whom is it permanent, if the first seller did not redeem it by the passage of a year? Rabbi Elazar says: it is permanent for the first buyer, for we count for him; for the first buyer we count twelve months; therefore it is right that it be permanently his.

messages.text: It belongs in perpetuity to the second buyer.

notes.he: שאין שמעון גואלה מלוי:
notes.en: It is permanent for the second: for Shimon cannot redeem it from Levi.

messages.text: Granted, according to the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, it is understandable why the house belongs to the first buyer, as one calculates the year according to his acquisition. But according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the reason that the house belongs to the second buyer after the conclusion of one year from the acquisition of the first buyer?
messages.quote: It belongs in perpetuity to the second buyer

messages.text: What did the first buyer sell to the second buyer? He sold him any right to the field that will come into his possession. This includes the fact that the house will belong to him in perpetuity after the conclusion of one year from the first purchase.

notes.he: שיהא במקומו שיוחלט לו:
notes.en: Any right that will come into his hand: that he [the second buyer] stands in his place, so that it becomes permanently his.

messages.text: If one sold two houses of walled cities, one on the fifteenth day of the first month of Adar in a leap year, and the other one on the first day of the second Adar, then the halakha is as follows:

With regard to this house that he sold to him on the first day of the second Adar, once the first day of Adar of the next year arrives, it is counted as though a full year has elapsed. With regard to this house that he sold to him on the fifteenth day of the first Adar, it is not counted as though a full year has elapsed until the fifteenth day of Adar of the next year.

notes.he: דהאיכא מיום ליום וזה שמכר לו בט"ו באדר לא עלתה לו שנה עד ט"ו באדר לשנה הבאה ואע"ג דהשתא הוו י"ג חדש משום דמיום ליום בעינן מט"ו באדר לט"ו באדר:
notes.en: A year has passed for him: for there is [a full year] from day to day. But for the one he sold to him on the fifteenth of Adar, a year has not passed for him until the fifteenth of Adar of the next year, even though now it is thirteen months, because we require [a year] from day to day, from the fifteenth of Adar to the fifteenth of Adar.

notes.he: שבר"ח אדר מכר עכשיו כשהגיע לראש אדר אחר:
notes.en: A year has passed for him: for he sold on the New Moon of Adar; now, when the New Moon of the next Adar arrived.

messages.text: But let the first buyer say to the second: I preceded you and kindled a fire before you, i.e., I bought my house before you acquired yours. How, then, can you gain possession in perpetuity before me?
messages.quote: it is not counted as though a full year has elapsed until the fifteenth day of Adar of the next year

notes.he: לוקח ראשון ללוקח שני אנא קדים שחין נורא אני היסקתי ונשתמשתי בבית קודם ממך ושלך נחלט באחד באדר ושלי לא תיחלט:
notes.en: But let him say: the first buyer to the second buyer: “I preceded [you in] kindling the fire,” I heated and made use of the house before you, yet yours becomes permanent on the first of Adar and mine does not become permanent?

notes.he: זה שקנה בט"ו באדר ראשון לאותו שקנה בר"ח השני:
notes.en: But let him say: the one who bought on the fifteenth of the first Adar to the one who bought on the New Moon of the second.

notes.dh: אנא קדים שחין נורא מיקמי דידך
notes.he: כלומר אני הסקתי אש בביתי במדורתי קודם שהיסקתה אתה בביתך שאני קניתי קודם מפני מה נחלט לך ביתך קודם משיחלט אותו שלי שקניתי קודם:
notes.en: “I preceded you in kindling the fire”: that is, I lit a fire in my house, in my hearth, before you lit [one] in your house, for I bought first. Why does your house become permanently yours before mine, which I bought first, becomes permanent?

messages.text: This is due to the fact that the second buyer can say to him: You descended to the house during the intercalated month, i.e., the first Adar, and as it is taught in the mishna, the seller has the right to redeem the house for an entire year, including the intercalated month.

notes.he: נכנסת בחודש העיבור לפיכך תפסיד דתמימה כתיב ליתן לו חדש העיבור אבל אני לא נכנסתי בו:
notes.en: You descended into the intercalation: you entered [the house] in the intercalated month; therefore you lose, for “full” is written, to give him [the seller] the intercalated month. But I did not enter in it.

notes.he: שקנית בחודש העיבור בט"ו באדר הראשון גלית אדעתך דשנת עיבור את רוצה לחשוב הלכך לא נגמרה שנתה עד ט"ו באדר:
notes.en: For he says to him: “You descended into the intercalation”: you bought in the intercalated month, on the fifteenth of the first Adar; you revealed your intent that you want to reckon a leap year. Therefore its year is not completed until the fifteenth of Adar.

messages.text: If two lambs were born to a single owner, one on the fifteenth day of the first Adar, and the other one on the first day of the second Adar, then the halakha is as follows:

notes.he: והם בכורות ומוזהר להקריבן בתוך שנתן דכתיב (דברים טו) תאכלנו שנה בשנה:
notes.en: Two lambs were born to him: and they are firstborns, and he is commanded to offer them within their year, as it is written: “You shall eat it year by year” (Deuteronomy 15:20).

notes.he: לידע אי זה יש לו תורת איל קודם מחבירו ואיכ' דאמ' לענין צירוף גורן של מעשר בהמה דכתיב במעשר בהמה שנה היוצא השדה שנה שנה. למ"ה:
notes.en: Two lambs were born to him: to know which of them has the status of a ram before the other. And some say [it concerns] combining [lambs] into one pen for the animal tithe, as it is written regarding the animal tithe: “that which comes forth from the field year by year” (Deuteronomy 14:22). [The note ends with an abbreviation, למ״ה, whose meaning is unclear.]

messages.text: With regard to this lamb that was born on the first day of the second Adar, once the first day of Adar of the next year arrives, it is counted as though a full year has elapsed, and if it was a firstborn it should be sacrificed before that time arrives ab initio. With regard to this lamb that was born to him on the fifteenth day of the first Adar, it is not counted as though a full year has elapsed until the fifteenth day of Adar of the next year.
But let the lamb that was born first say to the other lamb: I preceded you and ate vegetables before you, i.e., I was born first.
messages.quote: this lamb that was born to him on the fifteenth day of the first Adar

messages.text: This is due to the fact that the second lamb can say to the first: You descended to the world during the intercalated month, which is added to the year, whereas I did not descend to the world during the intercalated month.
Why do I also need this second halakha? This halakha with regard to the lambs is identical to that halakha concerning the houses.

Lest you say that there, with regard to houses of walled cities, where it is written: “A full year” (Leviticus 25:30), this is indeed the halakha, but here, with regard to lambs, where it is not written: A full year, perhaps this is not the case; Rabbi Abba bar Memel therefore teaches us that by means of a verbal analogy between the words “year” and “year” the two cases derive their halakhot from each other. With regard to houses of walled cities, it is written: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him” (Leviticus 25:30), and it is written with regard to lambs: “Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year” (Exodus 12:5).

verse.he: שֶׂה תָמִים זָכָר בֶּן־שָׁנָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם מִן־הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן־הָעִזִּים תִּקָּחוּ׃
verse.en: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a yearling male; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats.

notes.he: ולא ליתיב ליה חדש העיבור וליסלקיה שנה בט"ו בשבט:
notes.en: Where “full” is not written: and [one would say] it does not give it the intercalated month, and its year would be completed on the fifteenth of Shevat.

notes.he: גבי בתי ערי חומה לרבות חדש העיבור:
notes.en: There, where “full” is written: regarding houses of walled cities, to include the intercalated month.

notes.he: כתיב גבי ערי חומה שנה וכתיב בטלאים שנה שה תמים זכר בן שנה מה להלן תמימה דהיכא דנחית לעיבורא מחשבין לו שנת עיבור אף הכא נמי:
notes.en: It teaches us that “year” “year” are derived from one another: “year” is written regarding walled cities, and “year” is written regarding lambs: “a lamb without blemish, a male of the first year” (Exodus 12:5). Just as there [it is] “full,” so that where he descended into the intercalation we reckon a leap year for him, so too here.

messages.caption: Rabbi Abba bar Memel’s two sales in a leap year: the house sold in First Adar becomes permanent later than the one sold in Second Adar. His two lambs are counted the same way.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: When it states: “A full year” (Leviticus 25:30), this serves to include the intercalated month in the year calculated from the sale. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: This serves to give the seller a year and its addition.
messages.quote: this serves to include the intercalated month

messages.text: One counts 365 days, in accordance with the number of days in a solar year, which are eleven more than in a lunar year.
messages.lead: With regard to this matter, the Sages taught in a baraita: “A full year”;

notes.he: בין בפשוטה בין במעוברת:
notes.en: In accordance with the number of days of the sun: whether in an ordinary year or in a leap year.

notes.he: היינו שנת הלבנה ומה שיתירים חדשי החמה על הלבנה י"א יום דהיינו שס"ה ימים שתהא תמימה בין ללבנה בין לחמה]:
notes.en: A year and its addition: that is, the lunar year and the amount by which the months of the sun exceed those of the moon, eleven days, which makes 365 days, so that it is full both by the moon and by the sun.

messages.text: One counts twelve months from day to day, and if an additional month was intercalated into the year, then the month was intercalated to the benefit of the seller, i.e., he has thirteen months to redeem his house.

notes.he: כמו שאנו קובעין אותן לשנת לבנה:
notes.en: Twelve months from day to day: as we fix them for a lunar year.

notes.he: למוכר דכתיב תמימה:
notes.en: It was intercalated for him: for the seller, since “full” is written.

messages.text: It becomes the property of the buyer in perpetuity. This is the halakha with regard to one who buys a house in a walled city and one to whom it is given as a gift, as it is stated: “In perpetuity [latzemitut]” (Leviticus 25:30). With regard to this matter, the Sages taught:
messages.quote: If the final day of the twelve-month period arrived and the house was not redeemed

notes.he: היה יכול לגאול כל י"ב חדש הנותן המתנה וכשיגיע י"ב חדש ולא נגאלה היתה חלוטה לו:
notes.en: And one to whom it is given as a gift: the giver of the gift could redeem it for all twelve months, and when twelve months arrived and it had not been redeemed, it became permanently his [the recipient’s].

messages.text: “Latzemitut” means in perpetuity; that is, the seller can no longer redeem the house against the buyer’s will, nor does it return to his possession in the Jubilee Year.
Another matter derived from this verse is that “latzemitut” serves to include a house given as a gift.
What is the reason, i.e., how is this derived from “latzemitut”? The verse could have stated tzemit, but instead it states tzemitut. The expanded term serves to include a house given as a gift.

notes.he: שהיה יכול לומר לצמות ואמר לצמיתות לרבות המתנה שנחלטת ואינה יוצאה ביובל כמכר:
notes.en: As it is stated “latzemitut”: it could have said “litzmut,” but said “latzemitut,” to include a gift, that it becomes permanent and does not go out in the Jubilee, like a sale.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this ruling? Ostensibly, it is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, as if it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, doesn’t he say with regard to the return of an ancestral field in the Jubilee Year that a gift is not like a sale, i.e., an ancestral field given as a gift does not return to the original owner in the Jubilee Year? Likewise, a house in a walled city given as a gift should not become the perpetual property of the buyer after twelve months.
messages.lead: The Sages said the above baraita before Rav Pappa, and then asked:

notes.he: במס' בכורות בפ' אחרון (דף נב:) מתנה אינה כמכר לחזור ביובל למי שנתנה:
notes.en: Doesn’t he say: in tractate Bekhorot, in the last chapter (52b), that a gift is not like a sale, to return in the Jubilee to the one who gave it.

notes.dh: דאי ר"מ הא אמר מתנה אינה כמכר
notes.he: י"ל דכיון דאינה כמכר אין בידו לגואלה לעולם אפי' תוך י"ב חדש ולפי זה מה שהקשינו בפ' המקדיש (לעיל ערכין כח:) כיון דכתיב אחוזת עולם היא להם היה לנו לומר שלא יתנו בתיהם במתנה אבל נוכל לפרש הכא דמתנה אינה כמכר ויכול הנותן לגאול לעולם אפי' אחר י"ב חדש ובהכי ניחא דיכולים כהנים ולוים ליתן לאחר בתיהם במתנה:
notes.en: For if it is Rabbi Meir, doesn’t he say that a gift is not like a sale: One can say that since it is not like a sale, it is never in his [the giver’s] power to redeem it, even within twelve months. And according to this, regarding what we asked in chapter HaMakdish (above, Arakhin 28b), that since it is written “for it is their everlasting possession,” we should have said that they may not give their houses as a gift: but we can explain here that a gift is not like a sale, and the giver can always redeem it, even after twelve months. And with this it is resolved that priests and Levites may give their houses to another as a gift.

notes.he: דאמר בפ' יש בכור לנחלה אלו שאינן חוזרין ביובל כו'. דכי היכי דסבר ר' מאיר דמתנה אינה כמכר לענין למיפק ביובל הכי נמי דלא הויא כמכר למיחלט:
notes.en: In accordance with whom? Not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says in chapter Yesh Bekhor LeNaḥala: “These do not return in the Jubilee,” etc. Just as Rabbi Meir holds that a gift is not like a sale with regard to going out in the Jubilee, so too it is not like a sale with regard to becoming permanent.

messages.text: You may even say that the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, and it is different here, as the Merciful One includes a house given as a gift through the term “latzemitut.”
messages.quote: not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir

notes.he: כדאמר לעיל צמית צמיתות:
notes.en: For the Merciful One included [the gift] with “latzemitut”: as was said above, “tzemit,” “tzemitut.”

messages.text: But consider the case of the Jubilee Year, as it is written: “In this year of Jubilee you shall return every man unto his possession” (Leviticus 25:13), and the Sages teach that this verse serves to include the gift, and yet Rabbi Meir does not include a gift. Rather, this baraita is certainly not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir.
messages.lead: The Sages said to Rav Pappa, and some say that Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rav Pappa:
messages.quote: it is different here, as the Merciful One includes a house given as a gift

verse.he: בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: In this year of jubilee, each of you shall return to your holding.

notes.he: תשובו איש אל אחוזתו ודרשינן (בפ"ט) (שם) לרבות את המתנה:
notes.en: “You shall return”: “you shall return every man to his possession,” and we expound [it there] to include the gift.

notes.he: אמרי ליה רבנן לרב פפא והא אמרינן התם בפרק יש בכור] דהא גבי יובל כתיב תשובו לרבות את המתנות ור"מ לא קא מרבי. דתשוב תשובו לא משמע ליה [לרבות] הכי נמי צמית צמיתות לא משמע ליה [לרבות המתנה אלא ודאי דלא כר' מאיר]:
notes.en: The Sages said to Rav Pappa: but we said there, in chapter Yesh Bekhor, that regarding the Jubilee it is written “you shall return” to include gifts, and Rabbi Meir does not include [them], for “tashuv,” “tashuvu” does not imply [to include] to him. So too “tzemit,” “tzemitut” does not imply to him [to include the gift]. Rather, it is certainly not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

messages.text: With regard to one who consecrates a house among the houses of walled cities, this individual may redeem it from the Temple treasury, and he may always redeem it, even after the first year, unlike a sale.

notes.he: שאינו נחלט להקדש לעולם ולקמן מפרש טעמא:
notes.en: And he may always redeem: for it never becomes permanently the Temple’s; and below [the Gemara] explains the reason.

notes.he: דאינה יוצאה לכהנים ביובל כשדה אחוזה:
notes.en: And he may always redeem: for it does not go out to the priests in the Jubilee like an ancestral field.

messages.text: If another redeemed the house from the possession of the Temple treasury, and the final day of the twelve-month period from its redemption arrived and the house was not redeemed by its owner, the house has become the property of the other individual in perpetuity.

notes.he: משלקחו מן הגזבר:
notes.en: The day of twelve months arrived: [counted] from when he bought it from the treasurer.

notes.he: אותו אחר דינו כלוקח שאם הגיע יום י"ב חדש ולא גאלה המקדיש נחלט לזה שגאלה מיד הקדש:
notes.en: Another redeemed it from the Temple: that other has the status of a buyer, so that if the day of twelve months arrived and the consecrator did not redeem it, it becomes permanently [the property of] the one who redeemed it from the Temple.

messages.text: From where is this matter derived?
messages.quote: the house has become the property of the other individual in perpetuity

messages.text: As the verse states: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him, then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity, throughout his generations; it shall not go out in the Jubilee” (Leviticus 25:30). The verse indicates that the house belongs in perpetuity to “the one who bought it,” even if he purchased it from the possession of the Temple treasury.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: דכתיב וקם את הבית וגו':
notes.en: (Another redeemed it: as it is written: “Shall stand, the house,” etc.

notes.he: והאחר דכתיב וקם הבית וגו'):
notes.en: And the other: as it is written: “Shall stand, the house,” etc.)

messages.text: But why is the consecrator always capable of redeeming the house from the possession of the Temple treasury? Let it belong to the Temple treasury in perpetuity if it is not redeemed within one year.
messages.quote: and he may always redeem it

notes.he: ויהא חלוט להקדש אם לא נגאל בתוך שנתו למה גואל לעולם:
notes.en: And let the Temple make it permanent: and let it be permanently the Temple’s if it is not redeemed within its year; why may he always redeem it?

messages.text: The verse states: “Throughout his generations.” Excluded, therefore, is the Temple treasury, as it is not a person and it does not have generations.

notes.he: דליכא פריה ורביה קמי שמיא:
notes.en: Which has no generations: for there is no procreation before Heaven.

notes.he: למי שיש לו תולדות [דורות] יוצא לצמיתות:
notes.en: The verse states: “Throughout his generations”: for one who has offspring [generations], it goes out in perpetuity.

messages.text: Why do I need the phrase in the above verse: “It shall not go out in the Jubilee”? After all, it already stated: “In perpetuity.”

notes.he: הואיל וכתיב לצמיתות:
notes.en: Why do I need “it shall not go out in the Jubilee”: since “in perpetuity” is written.

notes.he: לא יצא ביובל דאינו חוזר לבעלים למה לי:
notes.en: “It shall not go out in the Jubilee,” that it does not return to the owners: why do I need it?

messages.text: This phrase is necessary only for the case of one who sells a house among the houses of walled cities and the Jubilee Year arrived during the year of the sale. It might enter your mind to say that the house should leave the possession of the buyer to enter the possession of its owner in the Jubilee Year. Therefore, the verse teaches us: “It shall not go out in the Jubilee,” to teach that this is not the case.

notes.he: דפקע יובל לקנינו קמ"ל דלא:
notes.en: It might enter your mind to say it should go out in the Jubilee: for the Jubilee cancels his acquisition; it teaches us that it does not.

messages.text: Mishna
At first, the buyer would conceal himself on the final day of the twelve-month period, in order to ensure that it would become his in perpetuity.

notes.he: הלוקח ביום שנים עשר חודש כדי שלא ימצאהו מוכר ליתן לו מעותיו והוא חלוט לו:
notes.en: Mishna. Would conceal himself: the buyer, on the day of the twelve months, so that the seller would not find him to give him his money, and it would be permanently his.

notes.he: יום י"ב חדש כדי שלא ימצאנו המוכר שיגאלנה ממנו כדי שיחלוט לו]:
notes.en: The buyer would conceal himself: on the day of the twelve months, so that the seller would not find him to redeem it from him, so that it would become permanently his.

messages.text: Hillel instituted that the seller would place [ḥolesh] his money in the chamber of the court and that he will break the door and enter the house, and when the other individual, i.e., the buyer, will wish to do so, he may come to the chamber and take his money.

notes.he: כמו (ישעיהו י״ד:י״ב) חולש על גוים וכדגרסינן (שבת דף קמח:) מטילין חלשים על הקדשים. שיהא מטיל מעותיו ללשכות שבעזרה:
notes.en: That he would place [ḥolesh]: as in “who casts lots [ḥolesh] over the nations” (Isaiah 14:12), and as we read (Shabbat 148b): “One casts lots [ḥalashim] over the sacrificial portions.” That he would cast his money into the chambers that are in the Temple courtyard. [The Davidson English renders “the chamber of the court.”]

notes.he: של בית שמכר ונכנס:
notes.en: And he would break the door: of the house that he sold, and enter.

notes.he: הכא משמע דבימי הלל שהיה בבית שני כדאמרינן בפ"ק דשבת (דף טו. ושם) הלל ושמעון גמליאל ושמעון נהגו נשיאותן לפני הבית מאה שנה היו נוהגין יובל כיון דבתי ערי חומה היה נוהג כדאמר בפירקין דלעיל (ערכין דף כט.) דאין בתי ערי חומה אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג וקשה לפירש"י דפרק השולח (גיטין דף לו.) דתנן הלל תיקן פרוזבול ופריך בגמ' עלה מי איכא מידי דאורייתא משמטא והתקין הלל דלא תשמט ומשני בשביעית בזמן הזה דרבנן ופרש"י והלל כרבי סבירא ליה דאמר שביעית להשמטת מלוה בזמן הזה דרבנן ואע"ג דהלל בבית שני הוה סבירא ליה דבבית שני הואיל ולא היה יובל נוהג לא היה נוהג שמיטה מדאורייתא ודאמרינן מנו יובלות לקדש שמיטין מדרבנן קאמר וכאן משמע דבבית שני היה יובל נוהג מן התורה וכן משמע בכריתות פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה בסופו (דף יא.) ויתנו ידיהם להוציא (את) נשיהם ואשמים וגו' אמר רב חסדא מלמד שכולן שפחה חרופה בעלו ושפחה חרופה היינו חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין המאורסת לעבד עברי ואמרינן בפרקין דלעיל (ערכין דף כט.) דאין עבד עברי נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג אלמא נהגו יובלות בבית שני וצ"ל דע"כ דאין הכי נמי דנהגו יובלות בבית שני ואע"ג דכל ישראל לא חזרו בימי עזרא כדכתיב (נחמיה ז׳:ס״ו) כל הקהל כאחד ארבע רבוא אלפים שלש מאות וששים ומיהו מכל שבט ושבט חזרו מקצתן והוי שפיר כמו כל יושביה עליה כדאמרינן לקמן שמנו יובלות אע"ג דלא חזרו כולן וההיא דפרק השולח (גיטין דף לו.) צ"ל דהלל לאו לדריה תקין אלא יודע היה שהבית היה עתיד ליחרב ולפיכך תיקן פרוזבול ואע"ג דבעי התם הלל כי תקין פרוזבול לדריה הוא דתקין או לדרי עלמא תקין ההיא לאו לאביי קבעי כי אם לרבא דמתרץ התם הפקר ב"ד היה הפקר:
notes.en: In brief: Hillel instituted: this implies that in the days of Hillel, who lived in the Second Temple period (as Shabbat 15a says: Hillel, Shimon, Gamliel and Shimon held their presidency for a hundred years before the Temple’s destruction), the Jubilee was in force, since the law of houses of walled cities was in force, and the previous chapter (Arakhin 29a) says that houses of walled cities apply only when the Jubilee is in force. This is difficult for Rashi’s explanation in Gittin 36a. There the mishna says Hillel instituted the prosbul, and the Gemara asks whether, where the Torah cancels a debt, Hillel could institute that it not be cancelled; it answers that the Sabbatical Year nowadays is rabbinic. Rashi explains there that Hillel holds like Rabbi, that the Sabbatical cancellation of debts nowadays is rabbinic, and that even in the Second Temple period, since the Jubilee was not in force, the Sabbatical Year did not apply by Torah law, and the statement that they counted Jubilees to sanctify Sabbatical Years means by rabbinic law. Yet here it is implied that the Jubilee applied by Torah law in the Second Temple period, and so too in Keritot 11a: on “and they gave their hands to put away their wives, and being guilty…” (Ezra 10:19), Rav Ḥisda says that all of them had relations with a designated maidservant, that is, half maidservant and half free, betrothed to a Hebrew slave; and the previous chapter (29a) says the Hebrew slave applies only when the Jubilee is in force. Evidently they observed Jubilees in the Second Temple period. Tosafot conclude that indeed they did, even though not all of Israel returned in Ezra’s day, as it is written: “The whole congregation together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty” (Nehemiah 7:66); some of each tribe returned, and that counts as “all its inhabitants upon it,” as is said below that they counted Jubilees even though not all returned. And Gittin 36a must mean that Hillel did not institute the prosbul for his own generation, but knew that the Temple would be destroyed and therefore instituted it. Although the Gemara there asks whether Hillel instituted the prosbul for his generation or for all generations, that question is asked not according to Abaye but only according to Rava, who answers there that the court’s declaring property ownerless is effective. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: העשויה לכך היה מניח מעות [פדיונו] באותו לשכה כשאינו מוצא הלוקח:
notes.en: That he would place [ḥolesh] his money in the chamber: [the one] made for that purpose; he would put the money [of his redemption] in that chamber when he could not find the buyer.

notes.he: פתח הבית שמכר ויכנוס בו וכשירצה הלה הלוקח יבא ויטול מעותיו מן הלשכה]:
notes.en: And he would break the door: the entrance of the house he sold, and enter it; and when the other, the buyer, wishes, he will come and take his money from the chamber.

messages.text: Gemara

It may be inferred from the ordinance of Hillel in the mishna that if one says to his wife: This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you will give me two hundred dinars, and she gave the money to him with his consent, then she is divorced. But if she gave it to him against his will, she is not divorced.
messages.quote: Hillel instituted that the seller would place his money in the chamber

notes.he: שיקבלם ברצון:
notes.en: Gemara. With his consent: that he accepts them willingly.

notes.he: שהטילתם בביתו כי ה"ג דתקין הלל במתני':
notes.en: Against his will: that she threw them into his house, in the same way as Hillel instituted in the mishna.

notes.he: מתקנתו של הלל ש"מ דנתינה בעל כרחו בעלמא לא הויא נתינה:
notes.en: From Hillel’s enactment, conclude that giving against his will is, in general, not giving.

messages.text: Continues on 32a: the Gemara explains Rava’s inference. Since Hillel needed an enactment to make giving against the recipient’s will count as giving, in general it does not count.
